CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A

  APRIL 2024 AGENDA

MEMBERS
Barbara Hibler, Chairperson  Peter Puglese, Public Works Department, City Traffic Engineer
Richard Galindo, District 1  Diana Maximo, Parking and Traffic Department (LAZ Parking)
Kip Rudd, District 2  William Thompson, Parking and Traffic Department (LAZ Parking)
Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3  Lieutenant David Salcedo, Police Department
Lois Hale, District 4

Rules of Decorum
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/DocumentCenter/View/18857/2023-Rules-of-Decorum

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
1. Roll Call

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEMS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any item on the agenda, other
  than the Public Hearing, may do so at this time.

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1. Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on March 27, 2024. See pages 3-6 of this agenda
  packet.

D. RESOLUTION
1. Staff report recommending that the Traffic and Parking Commission approve the resolution to
  terminate the Residential Parking Permit Program for Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue
  and approximately 132 feet south of 118th Place. See pages 7-34 of this agenda packet.

E. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. City-owned parking facilities as parking meter zones with special event parking rates and fines
a. The staff report can be obtained at https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Item/16627?fileID=23655
  Oral status report on the City-owned parking facilities

F. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

G. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on
  City related travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of
  general interest to the public.

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A

  MARCH 2024 MEETING MINUTES

A. OPENING CEREMONIES
 Chairperson Hibler welcomed the commission and the public for their attendance and participation.
 Meeting was held at 7:05 pm (PST) in the Community Room A located in the first floor on 02/28/24
 Attendees included Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett C.S. Roberts, Lois Hale, Peter
  Puglese, and William Thompson.
 Miss Katrina Gamez acted as Secretary to assist and attend the Parking and Traffic Commission.

B. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING AGENDA ITEM
 None

C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1. Approval of the Minutes for the Meeting held on February 28th, 2024
 A motion to accept the meeting notes was made by Richard Galindo and seconded by Kip Rudd.
 The motion was carried by the following roll call vote: Barbara Hibler, Richard Galindo, Kip Rudd, Brett
  Roberts and Lois Hale. All commissioners approved the minutes of the meeting notes. There was no
  rejection or noes.

D. PUBLIC HEARING
1. None

E. UNFINISHED BUSINESS
1. City-owned parking facilities as parking meter zones with special event parking rates and fines
a. The staff report can be obtained at HTTPS://WWW.CITYOFINGLEWOOD.ORG/AGENDACENTER/VIEWFILE/ITEM/16627?FILEID=23655
  Oral status report on the implementation plan for event parking rates and fines at public parking facilities
  and a timeline on when a draft plan will be completed for Commission review and comment.
 No Update at this time. Commissioners will follow this issue and ask questions when necessary.

2. Performance reports for the parking and shuttle service utilizing city-owned parking facilities
a. A shuttle performance report for the September-December 2023 NFL season and the latest quarterly
  report that would include other events that utilized the shuttle system.
 William Thomson recommended visiting https://inglewoodparkgo.com to become familiar with using the
  shuttle. Commissioners will follow this issue and ask questions when necessary.

F. PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS
1. Persons wishing to address the Parking and Traffic Commission on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.
 The resident of 117th Street made the following comments.
   There is no enforcement for speeding vehichles.
   The parking program does not support personal events and parties.
   The parking program is against providing a greater number of permits available per household.
   Others favor the parking program because of the accessibility of street parking to residents and
  visitors.

G. CHAIRPERSON AND COMMISSIONERS REMARKS
1. The members of the Parking and Traffic Commission will provide oral reports, including reports on City
  related travels where lodging expenses are incurred, and/or address any matters they deem of general
  interest to the public.
 Commissioners thanked William Thompson and crew for helping direct traffic during the noisy event.
 Commissioners asked about the timing of the traffic signal lights on Florence Avenue and High Street
  and High Street and Redondo Blvd. It was responded that the timing cannot be changed due to Metro
  Light Rail.
 Comissioners asked about no left turn signal from West Blvd onto Florence Avenue. It was responded
  that this is not a light controlled by City Of Inglewood. It is a light owned by City of LA. Public Works
  staff stated that the City of Los Angeles will be contacted regarding signal timing and informed of the
  issue.
 Comissioners asked about signal traffic timing on Century Blvd and Crenshaw Blvd. They were informed
  that due to construction, signal timings have been adjusted.

H. ANNOUNCEMENTS
1. It was announced that the next Traffic and Parking Commission meeting will be Wednesday, April 24,
  2024 at 7:00 p.m. m., 1st Floor, City Hall Community Room A, Inglewood City Hall One Manchester
  Boulevard, Inglewood, CA 90301

I. ADJOURNMENT
1. The Parking and Traffic Commission meeting ended at 7:37 PM PST.

J. ATTACHMENT
1. Attendance Sheet

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Public Works Department
DATE:  Wednesday, April 24, 2024

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Adoption of Resolution Recommending Termination of Residential Permit
  Parking Program for Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and
  approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place

RECOMMENDATION:
It is requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this
report and approve the resolution recommending that the City Council adopt an ordinance to
terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program within District 11 on Christopher Avenue
between Lemoli Avenue and approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place.

BACKGROUND:
On June 16, 2020, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 20-90 to implement a Citywide Permit
Parking Districts Program to cover all streets within the Permit Parking Districts map
accompanying the Ordinance. The program is designed to reduce traffic and parking impacts
to residential neighborhoods by non-resident vehicles parking in the area while attending events
at the City’s venues. The Ordinance grants the Public Works Director the authority to determine
whether permit parking restrictions apply 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, or any portion thereof.
The City must post signs of the permit parking restrictions.

Inglewood Municipal Code section 3-76 & 3-76.1 provide that residents and/or business persons
in a neighborhood may petition for the termination of a Permit Parking District by submitting a
petition bearing the signatures of at least 10 adults from different households and/or businesses.

On August 29, 2023, Public Works Department received a petition requesting the removal of
Residential Permit Parking on Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and approximately
132-ft South of 118th Place within District 11. There is a count of thirty-seven (37) properties
that are within the boundaries. Twenty-six (26) valid signatures were submitted on the petition.

Accordingly, on January 9, 2024, a notice was sent to all addresses within the petition boundary
to attend the January Traffic and Parking Commission meeting to express their views on the
matter.

DISCUSSION:
On January 24, 2024, the Parking and Traffic Commission held a public hearing on the issue of
terminating the Residential Permit Parking Program for Christopher Avenue between Lemoli
Avenue and approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place within District 11. The Parking and Traffic
Commission listened to public comments and all district commissioners voted to approve the
request to send questionairres to addresses in the affected district.

On February 1, 2024, the Public Works Department mailed questionaries to each resident
residing in the boundary area of the petition and requested the questionnaires be returned within
thirty (30) calendar days. For the parking restrictions to be removed, a minimum of seventy-five
percent (75%) of the returned questionnaires must be in favor of the removal (IMC § 3-76(a)).

On March 12, 2024, the questionnaires were counted. The City received thirty-two votes, with
twenty-nine (29) votes cast to approve the termination and three (3) votes opposed the
termination of the Residential Permit Parking Program, i.e., ninety-one percent (91%) of
households supported the removal of Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and
approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place from Permit Parking District 11.

Based on the results, Public Works staff recommends that the Parking and Traffic Commission
approve the resolution recommending that the City Council adopt an ordinance terminating the
Residential Permit Parking Program for Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and
approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place within District 11.

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Termination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 11 on Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and
approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place. Per Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code,
this matter will be presented to the Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place
specified:

  Wednesday January 24, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some
on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a
nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District
11 on Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place
would be warranted. If it is determined to be warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within
the subject area.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will
not be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you
have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the
public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de

Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la terminación
del permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 11 en Christopher Avenue entre Lemoli
Avenue y aproximadamente 132 pies al Sur de 118th Place.

De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este asunto se presentará
a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 24 de Enero de 2024 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones dentro del área de asunto. Cualquier persona
interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es dar a todos los residentes del área mencionada anteriormente la
oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema.

El propósito del Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para
los residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde
los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de
estacionamiento disponibles en la calle. La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo
tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada y si se
justificaría la terminación de un permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 11 en
Christopher Avenue entre Lemoli Avenue y aproximadamente 132 pies al Sur de 118th Place. Si se
determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del área en cuestión.

Si se rescinde un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no todos los residentes y visitantes
de este vecindario tendrán restricciones para estacionar en las calles públicas en cualquier momento;
incluso durante eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una
opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras Públicas
de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.

To:  Residents of Christopher Avenue

Subject:  Vote to Approve OR Reject the termination of Residential Permit Parking on
  Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and approximately 132-ft South of
  118th Place within District 11

The purpose of this letter is to allow residents the opportunity to vote on the removal of the residential
permit parking on Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and approximately 132-ft South of
118th Place within District 11.

By voting "approve", this street will not be subject to the rules of a Residential Permit Parking District.
By voting "reject", this street will continue to have permit parking and follow the rules associated with it.
The complete rules and procedures can be found in the Inglewood Municipal Code Section 3-76
(Establishment of a Permit Parking District) through Section 3-76.1 (Amending or Terminating a Permit
Parking District).

Since the Parking and Traffic Commission has determined that permitted parking may not be warranted
in the area in question, ballots are mailed to all residences within the boundary of the subject street.

If seventy-five percent (75%) or more of the returned ballots vote “approve” for the termination of
residential permit parking, then an ordinance amending the Residential Permit Parking District will be
submitted to the City Council for consideration. If approved, on Christopher Avenue between Lemoli
Avenue and approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place within District 11 will not be subject to the
Residential Permit Parking District rules. Therefore, all vehicles can park on these streets without
showing a parking permit at all hours of the day, every day of the week. Additionally, the current
parking prohibitions for street sweeping will remain unchanged.

Using the enclosed ballot, please vote to approve or reject the termination of the residential permit
parking on Christopher Avenue between Lemoli Avenue and approximately 132-ft South of 118th Place
within District 11. Please return the ballot to the City of Inglewood Public Works Department within
thirty (30) days from the date of this letter. Only one vote per household will be accepted. If you have
any questions, please do not hesitate to get in touch with the Public Works Department, at (310) 412-
5333.

Yours Truly,

El propósito de esta carta es brindarles a los residentes la oportunidad de votar sobre la eliminación
del permiso de estacionamiento residencial en Christopher Avenue entre Lemoli Avenue y
aproximadamente 132 pies al sur de 118th Place dentro del Distrito 11.

Al votar "aprobar", esta calle no estará sujeta a las normas de un distrito de estacionamiento con
permiso residencial. Al votar "rechazar", esta calle seguirá teniendo permiso de estacionamiento y
seguirá las reglas asociadas a la misma. Las reglas y procedimientos completos se pueden
encontrar en el Código Municipal de Inglewood, Sección 3-76 (Establecimiento de un Distrito de
Estacionamiento con Permiso) hasta la Sección 3-76.1 (Modificación o Terminación de un Distrito
de Estacionamiento con Permiso).

estacionamiento permitido no esté garantizado en el área en cuestión, las boletas se envían por
correo a todas las residencias dentro de los límites de la calle en cuestión. Si el setenta y cinco por
ciento (75%) o más de las boletas devueltas votan "aprobar" la terminación del permiso de
estacionamiento residencial, entonces se presentará al Concejo Municipal para su consideración
una ordenanza que modifica el Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial. Si se
aprueba, en Christopher Avenue entre Lemoli Avenue y aproximadamente 132 pies al sur de 118th
Place dentro del Distrito 11 no estará sujeto a las reglas del Distrito con Permiso de
Estacionamiento Residencial.

Por lo tanto, todos los vehículos pueden estacionar en estas calles sin mostrar un permiso de
estacionamiento a todas horas del día, todos los días de la semana. Además, las prohibiciones de
estacionamiento actuales para el barrido de calles se mantendrán sin cambios. Usando la boleta
adjunta, vote para aprobar o rechazar la terminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial
en Christopher Avenue entre Lemoli Avenue y aproximadamente 132 pies al sur de 118th Place
dentro del Distrito 11. Devuelva la boleta al Departamento de Obras Públicas de la Ciudad de
Inglewood dentro de los siguientes treinta (30) días. Sólo se aceptará un voto por hogar. Si tiene
alguna pregunta, no dude en comunicarse con el Departamento de Obras Públicas al (310) 412-
5333.
